a single work, as there is ample evidence that he had read widely in both the Confessions and

re-reading this work in January and February 1822 (Mary Jnl i 389–90, 394–7).
 The Rousseau figure may be considered to have three related purposes in TL. The first
is structural, as the narrator of the second vision, which creates the cyclical scheme of the
poem (see Structure). The second is chronological: the figure of Rousseau, who died in
1778 and whose remains were exhumed and placed in the Panthéon in 1794, allows a poem
which ranges across time from Aristotle to Napoleon to focus predominantly on the fifty
